clue.text: 7 35's Director?

parts.note: 7 and 35 together name the famous Georgian furniture designer, and the question mark invites reading a director as someone who heads a seat-maker's trade

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asking who directs a man named in two other entries.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: Thomas Chippendale (7 and 35) made chairs, so he was literally a 'chair person', while the everyday word means whoever chairs a board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who presides over a meeting or board is its director in a loose sense, and Chippendale made chairs.

clue.text: Smart man on board, a young singer

parts.note: smart in the stylish sense is chic
K is the king, a man on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A dapper chess-playing fellow is also a promising young vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' points to a chess piece, here the king, K.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby bird, which will grow up to sing, is called this; it is also slang for a young woman.

clue.text: On a plane where Bill eats pig flesh?

indicators.note: one word eating another holds it inside, so the bill surrounds the pig

parts.note: a bill or advertisement is an ad
boar is the wild pig, and its meat goes by the same name

explanation.surface: A traveller called Bill tucks into pork during a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard an aircraft means being on it as a passenger.

clue.text: Singer, having turned soprano, gives up

indicators.note: the letters of the word singer are turned about into a new order

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: A vocalist who has switched to singing soprano quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having turned' rearranges SINGER into RESIGN; S for soprano is then added.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a job or post formally is to resign, so gives up is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rare outing: corporation's mistake

indicators.note: an outing sends the letters of rare out and about into a new order

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A company's rare day out turns out to be an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outing' rearranges RARE into ERRA. 'Corporation' is dated British humour for a pot belly, hence TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin word names an error in print, usually listed on a correction slip in a book.

clue.text: Gives aid to gullible people, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for gullible folk is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: people easily fooled are suckers

explanation.surface: Someone helps out the easily duped.
explanation.definitionFit: To succour is to help someone in need, a literary synonym for giving aid.

clue.text: Relating to the birth of an ass?

definitions.meaning: the usual adjective for things concerning birth, as in a birth chart
the same word in anatomy relates to the nates, the buttocks, a cheeky sense of ass

explanation.surface: A question about a donkey foal's birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ass' looks like a donkey, but the second sense is the backside: in anatomy the nates are the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both birth and, in anatomy, the buttocks, giving two meanings.

clue.text: Chap with stomach upset after taking cocaine

indicators.note: an upset stomach is a churned one, so its letters are jumbled
after taking away the drug, its letter no longer joins the jumbled pool

parts.note: C is common slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A man suffers an upset stomach after using cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C (cocaine) from STOMACH and rearrange the rest; 'after taking' is a removal, not an addition.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so any man or chap could carry it.

clue.text: Group with black horse — Clive, Marie, Sian and Harold, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the British banking group whose logo is a black horse

definitions.text: Clive, Marie, Sian and Harold, perhaps
definitions.meaning: cricketer Clive, music-hall star Marie, TV weather presenter Sian and silent-film comic Harold all share this surname

explanation.surface: A list of famous people linked with a black horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Lloyds is a major British bank with a black horse emblem; the four people are famous namesakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname in the plural covers four famous bearers, and also names a bank group.

clue.text: Revolting German article in Manx dwelling-place

indicators.note: in places the German article inside the shortened dwelling
a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a house is a place to dwell
ein is German for a or an

explanation.surface: A German item found in an Isle of Man home is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx cat has no tail, so 'Manx' tells you to cut off the last letter; 'in' then puts the German article inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A heinous crime is shockingly wicked, so revolting fits as a strong synonym.

clue.text: Verbal account of revolting article

indicators.note: revolting letters turn over and rise up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes a disgusting item in words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' rearranges ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a spoken narration or detailed telling of events.

clue.text: See 33
See guest has forgotten us

indicators.note: forgetting the letters means leaving them out of the word guest

explanation.surface: Someone notices a visitor has forgotten them.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a joke or point is to understand it, as when you say 'I see'.

clue.text: Town in Yorkshire, as its resident might say with passion

indicators.note: Yorkshire speech drops the initial h, so the word is said the local way

parts.note: doing something with passion is doing it hotly

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire town named the way a local would say it, fervently.
explanation.walkthrough: Otley is a market town in West Yorkshire; the Yorkshire accent drops the H of HOTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Otley is a real market town in the Wharfe valley in West Yorkshire.

clue.text: Person proficient in judo and cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word and to the other

explanation.surface: Someone skilled at both judo and bike riding.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the A of AND to the end. 'and' looks like a link word but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A dan is a black-belt grade in martial arts, and by extension one who holds it.

clue.text: Close relations lead to sex and a bowel condition

indicators.note: the lead of the word sex is its first letter

parts.note: IBS is irritable bowel syndrome

explanation.surface: Intimate relationships supposedly bring on a digestive complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibs is short for siblings, brothers and sisters, the closest family.

clue.text: Bottom layer might be laid here

definitions.meaning: the lowest stratum, as in a river or sea floor
where things are laid down, as bricks on mortar or a person to sleep

explanation.surface: A note on where the lowest layer is put down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a foundation stratum and a place where one is laid to rest.

clue.text: New inn tests alarm in Covent Garden street

indicators.note: a new version of these words reorders all their letters

explanation.surface: A newly opened pub sets off an alarm test in a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges INN TESTS ALARM. St Martin's Lane is a street in Covent Garden, central London, where Chippendale had his workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: This London street runs north from Trafalgar Square into the Covent Garden district.

clue.text: Set up drug and sex game

indicators.note: in a down entry setting something up raises it, reading the letters bottom to top

parts.note: E is ecstasy
it is a euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: Arranging drugs and a sex game sounds like a dodgy party.
explanation.definitionFit: In British sport a tie is a single knockout match, as in a cup tie.

clue.text: Country's unnamed nationalists

indicators.note: without its name, the country drops N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: Iran is a Middle Eastern country

explanation.surface: A country's anonymous nationalist movement.
explanation.walkthrough: N stands for name, so 'unnamed' takes N out of IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish Republican Army was a militant Irish nationalist organisation.

clue.text: Sheikh going short, surprisingly with nil capital

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the pooled letters are mixed into an unexpected order
going short means losing the final letter of the word sheikh

explanation.surface: A sheikh, oddly, is short of cash and has no capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going short' trims SHEIKH to SHEIK; 'surprisingly' then rearranges SHEIK plus NIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Ginger wine gets male dead drunk

parts.note: red is red wine
he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Ginger wine leaves a man completely drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges DEAD into ADED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger hair is red, so someone ginger has red-coloured hair.

clue.text: Right old clown, in 18th-century style

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown

explanation.surface: A real old clown dressed in eighteenth-century fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a well-known British circus clown of the 20th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the ornate decorative style of the 1700s, which Chippendale's furniture often followed.

clue.text: Bureau assistant's last work computer

parts.note: a bureau is a writing desk

indicators.note: the last of the word assistant is its final letter

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An office helper's final job on a desk computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A desktop is a personal computer designed to sit on a desk.

clue.text: Cavalryman a drongo irritated

indicators.note: irritated letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier on horseback is annoyed by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritated' rearranges A DRONGO; drongo is Australian slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a mounted infantryman, later a cavalry soldier.

clue.text: See 17
Team Maker is here today

definitions.meaning: a side of ... players, as in cricket or football
the clue word Maker is entered at number 11 in today's grid

explanation.surface: A team says its manufacturer is present today.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading refers to the grid: Maker is the 11-across part of the long answer at 33.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has eleven players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Character of superior hotel

indicators.note: of indicates letters taken from part of the phrase superior hotel

explanation.surface: A description of a luxury hotel's character.
explanation.definitionFit: A character here means a letter, and rho is the Greek letter R.

clue.text: Exaggerated answer given by state capital

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means exaggerated
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: A state capital gives an over-the-top reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Raises poultry

definitions.meaning: tilts up, as one lifts an ear or a hat brim

explanation.surface: Someone farms chickens.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for tilting upward and the plural of a male farmyard bird.

clue.text: Young animal, one to see in 3D?

parts.note: a cub is a young fox, bear or lion
I is the Roman numeral one
the letter C is named like the word see

explanation.surface: A young animal is one worth watching in a 3D film.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cubic has three dimensions, as volume measured in cubes.

clue.text: Country home's vacated in spring

indicators.note: when home is vacated the letters for it leave the country's name

parts.note: Spain is a European country
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A country house left empty in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring, or a resort built around one.

clue.text: Propose docking of iPad?

indicators.note: docking means cutting off the tail, here the final letter

parts.note: an iPad is a tablet computer

explanation.surface: Suggesting you put an iPad in its dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docking' looks like plugging into a charging dock; it means cutting off the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage, to table a motion is to put it forward for discussion.

clue.text: Support tossing of caber

indicators.note: tossing throws the letters of caber into a new order

explanation.surface: Helping out at the Highland caber toss.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing the caber is a Scottish Highland games event, heaving a tree trunk end over end.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a support or prop, as in a back brace.

clue.text: 7.35? May now…

definitions.meaning: Thomas Chippendale, from 7 and 35, was a famous furniture craftsman
Theresa May, then Prime Minister, picked her team of senior ministers

explanation.surface: A cross-reference and a nod to the Prime Minister's reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019, and a Prime Minister chooses the Cabinet of senior ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippendale built fine cupboards and chests, and a Prime Minister forms the government's top team.

clue.text: …love to kiss a behind that's salty!

parts.note: O is a zero score, love in tennis
X is a kiss at the end of a letter
late means behind time

explanation.surface: Continuing the PM's story, love, a kiss and a cheeky behind make it racy.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxalate is a salt of oxalic acid, so it is salty in the chemical sense; the definition is loose.

clue.text: Stripper snapped topless, gyrating in S American country

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the country's name

parts.note: Chile is a South American country

indicators.note: gyrating letters whirl into a new order
topless drops the first letter of the word snapped

explanation.surface: A stripper is photographed topless while dancing in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter and 'gyrating' rearranges what remains before it goes in. The Chippendales are a famous troupe of male striptease dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Chippendales dance troupe are male strippers, named after the furniture maker.
